title: Memories may be active agents in the sense-making process

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Memories may be active agents in the sense-making process

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin speculates that, on a substrate-independent, processual view of life and mind, memories, as patterns in the excitable medium of cognitive systems, could be seen as minimally agential participants that help shape their own reinterpretation, blurring the line between thoughts and thinkers.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I also speculate that a substrate-independent, processual view of life and mind suggests that memories, as patterns in the excitable medium of cognitive systems, could be seen as active agents in the sense-making process.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “Abstract”. Scope: Cognitive systems in general

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-03: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.09

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Memory patterns can have measurable causal effects, but those effects are compatible with both agential and non-agential descriptions. The substrate-independent speculation therefore has no distinct empirical consequence as stated.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The statement supplies no criterion separating a memory pattern that is an active agent from the same causal dynamics described without agency language.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Minimal agency is undefined.

Causal influence by a memory does not by itself discriminate agency from mechanism.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.1
analysis feasibility: 0.15
data existence: 0.1
data adequacy: 0.05
discriminating power: 0.05

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The text presents this as a way memories could be seen on a processual view of mind. No measurement of neural, cellular, or network activity distinguishes an agential memory from a pattern being transformed by the system that stores it. The claim is not an empirical proposition that current data could settle.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Treating a memory trace as a minimally agential participant in its own reinterpretation does not specify an observation that would differ from ordinary dynamics of an excitable medium.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim is explicitly a speculation about how to see memories.

Agency of a pattern is not separable from the dynamics of the medium that carries it.
